question.text: A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is projected from the ground with an initial speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>u</mi><mo>∘</mo></msub></math> at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> with the horizontal. At the highest point of its trajectory, it makes a completely inelastic collision with another identical particle, which was thrown vertically upward from the ground with the same initial speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>u</mi><mo>∘</mo></msub></math>. The angle that the composite system makes with the horizontal immediately after the collision is

solution.text: At the highest point \(v_{1}=\frac{u_{0} \cos \alpha}{2} \quad\) (by applying momentum conservation in horizontal direction) \(\mathrm{v}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{u}_{0} \cos \alpha}{2} \quad\) (by applying momentum conservation in vertical direction) \(\theta=45^{\circ}\left(\mathrm{H}=\frac{\mathrm{u}_{0}^{2} \sin ^{2} \alpha}{2 \mathrm{~g}}\right)\)
